hints.title: Strictly Increasing Chain Length
hints.text: Because each value must strictly divide the next when changing values, a sequence of distinct elements has length at most 14 since 2^14 exceeds 10000.

hints.title: Dynamic Programming over Divisor Sequences
hints.text: Compute the number of strictly increasing sequences of length k ending at each value using dynamic programming over multiples.

hints.title: Combinatorial Placement
hints.text: A sequence with k distinct elements can be expanded into an array of length n in comb(n - 1, k - 1) ways using stars and bars.

hints.title: Chains and Combinations Implementation

variables: maxValue: upper bound on array values
n: length of the ideal array
complexity.notes: Harmonic series sum over multiples bounded by maxValue log maxValue.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Standard O(n * maxValue) DP state transitions are too slow for n up to 10^4.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Stores chain counts up to max chain length 14.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Combines harmonic divisor sieve dynamic programming with stars and bars combinatorics.
